speaker: Doctor
text: I am Dr. Agent. You present with fatigue, severe itching, and abnormal liver function tests; to begin our workup, have you noticed any yellowing of your eyes or skin, or dark urine recently?

speaker: Patient
text: 32-year-old male. The patient reports a 2-month history of increasing generalized fatigue and severe pruritus. He has known hypertension and was diagnosed with ulcerative colitis 5 years ago. He mentions being sexually active with 2 female partners and inconsistent condom use.

speaker: Doctor
text:
DIAGNOSIS READY: Primary Biliary Cholangitis (PBC) is less likely given the male gender and sexual history; the clinical picture of severe pruritus, fatigue, abnormal LFTs, and risk factors for blood-borne viruses suggests Hepatitis B or C, while Ulcerative Colitis raises the concern for Primary Sclerosing Cholangitis (PSC). I will prioritize ruling these out.

REQUEST TEST: Hepatitis_Serology (HBsAg, Anti-HBc, Anti-HCV), Antimicrosomal_Antibodies, Proliferating_Cell_Nuclear_Antibody (p-ANCA).
